tldr: Patanjali Foods Limited reported its Q2 and H1 FY27 results, recording operating revenue of INR11,323 crores for Q2 (up 16% YoY) and INR22,660 crores for H1. Growth was supported by strong performances in the edible oil and biscuits segments, despite headwinds from commodity inflation and rural demand pressures.
management_commentary: Revenue from operations for Q2 stood at INR11,323 crores, up 16% year-on-year, with operating EBITDA of INR426 crores.
First-half revenue from operations reached INR22,660 crores, up 22% year-on-year, with operating EBITDA of INR969 crores.
Edible oil segment achieved its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR8,532 crores, up 22% year-on-year.
FMCG quarterly revenue stood at INR2,923 crores with EBITDA of INR221 crores.

The government reduced the effective import duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil from 16.5% to 11%, and on crude sunflower oil from 16.5% to 5.5% on September 24th, which the company is passing on to consumers.
guidance: Expect to close the year at a broad basis 15% growth in HPC.
Expect commodity inflation to continue in the near term.

segment_performance.notes: Quarterly revenue of INR8,532 crores, up 22% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 3%. Half-year revenue stood at INR17,037 crores, up 25% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 4.11%.
Generated revenue of INR742 crores during the quarter.

Quarterly revenue stood at INR2,923 crores with EBITDA of INR221 crores at a margin of 7.57%. Half-year revenue stood at INR5,861 crores, up 15% YoY, with EBITDA at INR411 crores and a margin of 7.01%.
Quarterly revenue of INR638 crores, up 28% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 11.91%. Half-year revenue stood at INR1,198 crores, up 28% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 13.52%.
Generated revenue of INR839 crores in the quarter and INR1,949 crores in the half year.
Quarterly revenue of INR186 crores with volume-led growth of 16% YoY. Half-year revenue stood at INR345 crores, up 15% YoY.
Revenue of INR306 crores in the quarter and INR525 crores in the half year.
Quarterly revenue stood at INR21 crores in the quarter and INR59 crores in the half year.

notable_qa.question: Ashutosh from ICICI Securities asked about competitive intensity in the toothpaste and biscuit categories and the performance of herbal markets.
notable_qa.answer: Management stated that while competitive intensity is high in dental care due to new launches and pricing, Patanjali Dant Kanti grew 16% compared to Q1 (revenue of INR378 crores). In biscuits, growth is largely volume-led with distribution reach expanding to over 3 lakh direct outlets.

notable_qa.question: Abhishek Mathur from Systematix Group inquired about volume versus realization trends in biscuits, skincare, and edible oils, and reasons for decline in staples/ethnic foods.
notable_qa.answer: Management noted biscuits and skincare growth is primarily volume-led, while edible oil revenue growth is largely driven by unit price increases with about 3% volume growth. Staples saw a conscious decision to de-grow due to commodity inflation challenges to protect margins.

notable_qa.question: Dhiraj Mistry from Jefferies asked about inventory losses following import duty reductions in September.
notable_qa.answer: Management stated the impact was minimal because a large part of inventory was afloat or in bonded non-duty customs warehouses, and inventory is tracked daily with P&L adjustments accounted for within the same quarter.

notable_qa.question: Priya Kulkarni from CN Capital asked about the financial impact of edible oil packaging standardization.
notable_qa.answer: Management stated there is no negative financial impact as adequate time was given to run through existing packaging inventory.

risks: Steady rise in inflation through the quarter (from 4.45% in July to 6.09% in October) and high food inflation at 8.94%.
Monsoon ended with a 13% rainfall deficit, affecting Kharif harvest and Rabi sowing.
Muted rural demand amid inflationary pressures.
Rising commodity costs including wheat, sugar, milk procurement, soybean, crude-linked inputs, and logistics/freight costs.
